title: linear-transform-2d widget params
description: A self-contained 'drag the basis vectors' engine for 2D linear maps. The reader drags the two coloured handles — the tips of where the standard basis vectors î and ĵ land — and the 2x2 matrix M = [[a,b],[c,d]] whose columns are those images carries the whole integer grid to a sheared lattice, transforms the unit square (and an optional shape), and the readout reports M, det M = ad-bc (the signed-area scaling factor / the value of dx wedge dy on the image vectors), orientation, and invertibility. The renderer owns the drag gesture, the data<->pixel mapping, the grid/arrow drawing and Reset; the widget is fully param-driven (initialMatrix, optional shapePoints) with an optional bodyScript decorate hook for extras. The gesture is 'drag-basis' — a dimension the corpus otherwise lacks. jsdom-safe: createSVGPoint/getScreenCTM run only inside the pointer handlers, never at init.

widgetId.description: DOM id for the outer <div class="widget"> wrapper. The Reset button derives its id from it (widgetId+'-reset').

svgId.description: DOM id for the <svg> drawing surface.

outputId.description: DOM id for the .readout the engine writes M / det / orientation into.

hint.description: Optional hint in .hd > .hint. Should tell the reader to drag the two coloured handles.

svgTitle.description: Accessible <title> inside the SVG. Defaults to title.

range.description: Half-width of the data window: axes span [-range, range]. Default 5.

gridExtent.description: Integer grid lines drawn from -gridExtent to +gridExtent. Default 6.

initialMatrix.description: Initial 2x2 matrix [[a,b],[c,d]] (columns = images of î and ĵ). Reset restores it. Default [[1,0],[0,1]].

shapePoints.description: Optional polygon (in data coords) drawn and transformed alongside the unit square, e.g. to show how a figure deforms. Closed automatically.

bodyScript.description: Optional author JS defining `function decorate(m, helpers){ ... }` for extra overlays (eigenvectors, annotations). `m` is {a,b,c,d,det}; helpers exposes G (the SVG group, redrawn each frame), PX/PY (data->pixel), ap(x,y) (apply M), and the page-global $/SVG. Called at the end of every redraw. Must not start a timer.
